## Key takeaways

- **If the listener cannot hear it, it does not exist.** Every important action
  must reach the ear through dialogue, narration, sound effect, ambience, or
  music.

- **Visual vs. audio.** A visual screenplay can show actions; an audio screenplay
  must make them audible.

- **Scene-oriented format.** Each scene has AMBIENCE, NARRATOR, dialogue, and
  SFX, plus an educational outcome stated in closing narration.

- **Semantic sound design.** Each sound effect represents an event or state in
  the technical model — sound is part of the model, not decoration.

- **Narration and dialogue.** Dialogue carries relationships and state
  transitions; narration carries connective tissue and learning outcomes.

- **Pacing and transitions.** Give the listener time to absorb each outcome;
  end scenes on a note that leads into the next.

- **Fourth-wall breaks (optional).** Use sparingly to re-anchor a listener who
  has forgotten the mapping.

- **Intermediate representation.** The screenplay sits between knowledge and the
  rendered artifact. It must stay useful independently of the renderer.

## Producing screenplay.md

Your output from this module is `screenplay.md`. In the next module it becomes
the input to an audio production platform.
